item.title: Iran war live: Saudi coalition hits Houthi sites; Aramco office hit in east
item.description:
"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA), Republican Nominee for the US Senate from Louisiana, says high diesel prices are putting pressure on farmers during harvest season, with some producers talking about going under. Kevin Book, ClearView Energy Partners managing director, says additional Russian diesel is unlikely to offset the roughly 70% run-up in diesel prices, though he estimates increased volumes could provide roughly 5 to 20 cents a gallon in relief by the end of the fourth quarter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
item.description:
Theme park company Six Flags temporarily closed nine rollercoasters across six amusement parks on Monday after one person died and several others were injured in an incident involving a coaster in Georgia. Officials did not confirm how the person died, nor how the others were injured or their conditions. Witnesses who spoke to NBC affiliate WXIA of Atlanta said they saw a man fall from the Goliath rollercoaster. “He fell and hit the car three different times,” one witness told the station. Death on Six Flags rollercoaster in US triggers ride closures across six states Continue reading...

item.title: Elon Musk becomes biggest donor of US midterms cycle with $366m spent
item.description:
Over the weekend , a poorly constructed and very obviously fake claim about Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico sprang up on X only to almost instantly fall apart. The claim was that Talarico had been absent from the campaign trail not because he had the flu, as he and his campaign have said, but because he was secretly flown to Ohio on a private plane and committed to a mental hospital there. One of the most prominent people involved in spreading the story on X was none other than the site’s owner, Elon Musk. With the midterm elections just weeks away, Musk is pouring money into GOP Senate candidates’ coffers and involving himself in the spread of literal fake news about a Democratic candidate, at a time when basically every true trust and safety guardrail has long been erased from his site. Given that he and his companies stand to profit handsomely from a Republican…

item.title: Albanian police fire tear gas at protesters as Education Ministry attacked
item.description:
Climate activist Greta Thunberg joined student protesters in France on Tuesday after weeks of violent confrontations with police, thousands of arrests and widespread school closures over demands for education reform. The 23-year-old Swedish activist appeared outside a high school in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, where students were demanding more teachers, better facilities and shorter school days, Reuters reported. More than 6,800 people have been detained since the protests began in September, according to French authorities. Demonstrators have set fires, erected barricades and confronted riot police in cities across France, although many protests have remained peaceful. FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION Thunberg, who rose to prominence organizing school strikes over climate change , criticized the French government's response to the demonstrations. item.title: Intense waves and floods batter California waterfront homes and boardwalks
item.description:
Boardwalk destroyed in Long Beach and homes damaged, while Baja California in Mexico and Las Vegas also affected Southern California coastal communities are picking up the pieces after a weekend of extreme weather brought flooding that overtook city streets and intense waves battered beachside homes. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel hit Mexico ’s Baja California over the weekend as well as southern California and Las Vegas. While meteorologists noted that Rachel weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it approached California, it still left a trail of destruction. Continue reading...

item.title: In first visit to Ceuta, Spain's king asks for 'good faith' from Morocco after migration crisis
item.description:
King Felipe VI on Tuesday said Ceuta and Melilla were "an inalienable part" of Spain as he made a landmark visit to the north African territories claimed by neighbouring Morocco. "Ceuta and Melilla are an inalienable part of the political and national reality that is Spain. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of our country are not negotiable," Felipe said. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Texas woman uses state law to sue anti-abortion group that allegedly ordered abortion pills online
item.description:
In March, two Mother Jones videographers and I stood outside the Space Center Houston and watched Kristan Hawkins, president of Students for Life, order abortion pills online. We were shadowing Hawkins through Texas for a profile , documentary , and radio story about her role overseeing one of the anti-abortion movement’s most influential organizations, which now claims 1,700 chapters nationwide. On that spring day, we watched as Hawkins and a Students for Life spokesperson, Lydia Taylor Davis, attempted to show just how easy it was to obtain abortion pills in Texas, despite its stringent laws, in the hopes that state and federal officials would do more to stop the pills. Now, Hawkins has been sued over the stunt, under a 2025 state law she and her team publicly lobbied for that was meant to target abortion providers and advocates. item.title: Arsenal thrash Lille as Atletico Madrid beat Manchester United
item.description:

Bayern Munich were held to a shock 3-3 draw by Norway’s Viking after Michael Olise was sent off.
